## Implementation Plan for Adding DebuggerDisplay to Activity and Friends - [x] Explore repository structure and understand Activity class - [x] Build and test baseline to ensure all tests pass - [x] Add DebuggerDisplay attribute to Activity class with OperationName and Id - [x] Add DebuggerTypeProxy for Activity class to show Tags and Baggage collections - [x] Add DebuggerDisplay to ActivityContext struct - [x] Add DebuggerDisplay to ActivityLink struct - [x] Add DebuggerDisplay to ActivityEvent struct - [x] Add DebuggerDisplay to ActivitySource class - [x] Build the changes - [x] Add tests for debugger attributes (5 new tests) - [x] Run all tests to verify no regressions (402/402 tests pass) - [x] Run security scan (CodeQL - no issues found) - [x] Address feedback: Fix property grouping and move TagObjects to top - [x] Simplify collection properties using LINQ - [x] Use primary constructor and alphabetize properties - [x] Display collections with "Count = X" for better UX - [x] Use new List constructor and reusable test helpers - [x] Change DebuggerToString method to property - [x] Remove unnecessary comments and custom reflection from tests - [x] Use DebuggerDisplayString property in ActivityLink - [x] Final validation and cleanup ## Summary Successfully implemented DebuggerDisplay and DebuggerTypeProxy attributes for Activity and related types to improve the debugging experience. ### Changes Made 1. **Activity.cs**: - Removed `using System.Linq;` (no longer needed) - Added `[DebuggerDisplay("{DebuggerDisplayString,nq}")]` showing OperationName and Id - Changed from `DebuggerToString()` method to `DebuggerDisplayString` property for consistency with .NET patterns - Added `[DebuggerTypeProxy(typeof(ActivityDebuggerProxy))]` - Created `ActivityDebuggerProxy` class with: - **Primary constructor** for cleaner syntax - **Alphabetized properties** with no blank lines for better readability - **Collections as List** using `new List(collection)` constructor to display "Count = X" in debugger (more user-friendly) - **TagObjects**, **Baggage**, **Events**, **Links** as grouped properties - **Context** property exposed in the proxy - All collection properties using efficient `new List(...)` constructor 2. **ActivitySource.cs**: Added `[DebuggerDisplay("Name = {Name}")]` to show the ActivitySource name in debugger instead of default ToString() 3. **ActivityContext.cs**: Added `[DebuggerDisplay]` showing TraceId, SpanId, and TraceFlags 4. **ActivityLink.cs**: - Added `[DebuggerDisplay("{DebuggerDisplayString,nq}")]` showing Context TraceId and SpanId - Changed from using nested property access to `DebuggerDisplayString` property for consistency and testability 5. **ActivityEvent.cs**: Added `[DebuggerDisplay]` showing Name and Timestamp 6. **ActivityTests.cs**: - Updated tests to use reusable DebuggerAttributes helpers from Common test utilities - Removed all unnecessary comments - Removed all custom reflection code - Tests now rely entirely on the helper methods to validate debugger attributes 7. **System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource.Tests.csproj**: Added reference to Common test DebuggerAttributes helper ### Code Improvements **DebuggerDisplayString Property Pattern:** ```csharp // Activity [DebuggerDisplay("{DebuggerDisplayString,nq}")] private string DebuggerDisplayString { get { ... } } // ActivityLink [DebuggerDisplay("{DebuggerDisplayString,nq}")] private string DebuggerDisplayString => $"TraceId = {Context.TraceId}, SpanId = {Context.SpanId}"; ``` **Clean Tests:** ```csharp // All tests now use helpers - no custom reflection DebuggerAttributes.ValidateDebuggerDisplayReferences(activity); DebuggerAttributes.ValidateDebuggerTypeProxyProperties(activity); ``` **List Constructor Instead of LINQ:** ```csharp // Uses List constructor (no LINQ dependency) public List> TagObjects => new List>(activity.TagObjects); ``` ### Testing ✅ All 402 tests pass ✅ No security vulnerabilities (CodeQL scan clean) ✅ Builds successfully for all target frameworks ✅ No breaking changes to public API ✅ Collections display "Count = X" for better UX ✅ ActivitySource shows its Name in debugger ✅ No LINQ dependency in ActivityDebuggerProxy ✅ Tests use reusable Common test utilities ✅ DebuggerDisplay uses property pattern consistently across all types ✅ Clean test code without unnecessary comments or custom reflection ✅ ActivityLink uses DebuggerDisplayString property for testability The changes significantly improve the debugging experience for distributed tracing scenarios, making it easier for developers to inspect Activity objects and their related types.
